FlumeApi carries the stop-flag path rule

edit.description: optional contractTouching beside the package fields, with its hint
write the stop flag after a marked ship

summary: Package entry extension gains optional `contractTouching`; the default handoff writes the stop flag after shipping one

per.section: One tick is one fresh process

acceptance: A shipped entry marked `contractTouching` leaves the stop flag on disk; an unmarked ship leaves none. The ladder's own routing is unchanged in both cases.
tests: the default handoff writes the stop flag after a contractTouching entry ships
the default handoff writes no stop flag when no shipped entry is contractTouching
pins: the package entry extension accepts an entry that omits contractTouching
notes: The mechanism the cited section already points at — "its build handoff writing the stop flag after shipping an entry plan marked contract-touching". `.flume/PROTOCOL.md` rule 6's single-entry case is the operator's; it is outside every phase lane.

edit.description: read the worktree's tracked modifications after the agent exits, before teardown; carry them on the verdict

summary: Report on the tick verdict the tracked paths a tick modified and did not commit, before teardown removes the worktree

per.section: Tip verify — one writer per branch, absorption at the merge

acceptance: Every tick that ran an agent writes its uncommitted tracked paths on the verdict before teardown, so the loss is seen though not preserved.
tests: a tick that commits nothing reports the tracked paths it modified before teardown
a tick that left no tracked modification reports an empty set
notes: Read NUL-separated (.claude/rules/platform-facts.md, git's porcelain quoting). The fact is the engine's; what it means stays the chain's. The package's clean-tree gate re-runs `git status` today and is the fact's intended reader once it rides a gate-reachable surface — a later entry, not this one.

summary: Render the running lane's exclusions into plan's `tests[]` and `pins[]` hints — informed at authorship, never refused on a prediction
acceptance: Plan's rendered schema names the globs no judge will reach; no gate refuses an entry over its declared `files`.
tests: the tests[] hint names the globs the running lane excludes
the pins[] hint names the globs the running lane excludes
a running lane with no exclusions renders the hint without a lane clause
notes: `Runner.lanes` has shipped with no reader; this is the reader the cited section names. The hints stay tool-neutral — the globs come from the consumer's own declaration. `.flume/declaration.ts:61-63` still claims a plan-time refusal; that file is outside every phase lane.

edit.description: one clause in the named-lines paragraph

summary: State in plan's discipline that a `tests[]` line is judgeable only when the entry also changes a file not among the ones holding it
acceptance: The named-lines paragraph states the overlap condition, so a tests-only entry declares its behavior elsewhere or carries no `tests[]` line.
notes: Red-on-base lays the merged bytes of the files holding the named tests over the base checkout; for a tests-only diff that is the whole change, so the line passes at the base by construction. Five field instances. The lane half of the same wall is LANE-EXCLUDES-INFORM-THE-NAMED-LINE-HINTS.
